dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_store_stays_test_local`'s git-worktree-list guard robust to a nonzero git exit (catch subprocess.CalledProcessError and skip/degrade) so a store git can't fail cleanly and turn an unrelated test into a teardown ERROR.
evidence: tests/interfaces/conftest.py:250: `for p in worktree_paths(repo)` invoked from the autouse teardown, which runs for every store-bearing test in the tier
ABSENCE: no try/except around the `check=True` git invocation in the autouse teardown path, so a nonzero git exit raises instead of degrading to a skip or clean assertion
dropped.finding: The autouse tier-wide `_store_stays_test_local` teardown calls `worktree_paths(repo)` which runs `git worktree list --porcelain` with `check=True`, unguarded by try/except. It fires for every test whose REBAR_ROOT dir has both `.tickets-tracker` and `.git`. If any such test (e.g. a store-corruption or broken-worktree-pointer test among the ~20 module-local store fixtures) leaves git in a state where `worktree list` exits nonzero, the guard raises CalledProcessError in teardown and turns an otherwise-passing test into an ERROR, masking the real outcome.
dropped.suggested_fix: Wrap the `worktree_paths(repo)` call in the autouse teardown in a try/except subprocess.CalledProcessError and `return` (or record a soft note) on failure, so the safety-net guard never converts an otherwise-passing test into a teardown ERROR.
